invariants: Contract-only goal/workload variant: the objective switches from latency_ms to peak_allocated_bytes (bytes, minimize) on the identical source workload -- offline, batch 32 -- with the single goal constraint images_per_second >= 0.95 x the original baseline; switching the goal changes no workload dimension, input, asset, precision, seed, state, quality or measurement policy (request goal, objective, workload; README section 6 on distinguishing goal switching from input change).

One measured invocation is exactly one infer(model, pixels) call -- model(pixel_values=pixels).logits under torch.inference_mode() -- on the frozen GPU-resident 32 x 3 x 224 x 224 float32 batch (resnet_inference.py:14-16,45; request note 'One measured invocation'); the frozen evaluator's run(state) performs this single full forward and returns its complete 32 x 1000 FP32 logits tensor (adapter.py:78-86), unchanged by the goal switch.

Model is the pinned pretrained microsoft/resnet-18 revision 65a5785d9156231087c481e0c7dd33a5ff6f7e3e loaded locally (local_files_only=True) from request['assets'] with dtype=torch.float32, then eval(); no retraining, reinitialization, weight substitution or dtype change (resnet_inference.py:23; asset-manifest.json; adapter.py:46-52).

Inputs are the real preprocessed public images from pixels.npy (float32 NCHW 224, ImageNet mean/std, prepared offline per prepare_resnet_assets.py and asset-manifest.json); the workload batch is images[torch.arange(batch) % 3].contiguous() built once and GPU-resident before timing (resnet_inference.py:29; adapter.py:53-55); batch is read from request['workload']['batch'] (32 in this frozen run), never embedded as an adapter constant.

FP32 numerical, thread and RNG policies are fixed: dtype torch.float32, TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark=False, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', inference_mode execution, torch.manual_seed(20261020), 4 CPU threads, interop 1 (common.py:34-42; resnet_inference.py:14,23; request note 'Numerical policies preserved'; adapter.py:24,27-39).

Correctness is reference fidelity of the complete output: all 32 x 1000 FP32 logits compared with logits_atol=logits_rtol=1e-4, argmax(-1) predicted classes exactly equal (require_exact_top1), and a +1-corruption negative control rejected by the closeness check (workloads.json resnet_inference.correctness; common.py:74-84; resnet_inference.py:31-33); the frozen evaluator runs these relational checks in observe() outside timed run(), including a repeated full forward that must be close within tolerance and top-1 identical (adapter.py:99-117); no accuracy or tolerance is loosened by the goal switch.

Timing and memory-statistics boundaries match the source: model loading, input staging/host-to-device transfer, reference construction, correctness checks, warmup (2) and repeats (5) are outside the measured call; each measured call is bracketed by torch.cuda.synchronize() with torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats() immediately before it and the peak read after the closing synchronize, per measurement_lifetime 'invocation' (resnet_inference.py:38-47; request measurement fields; README measurement section).

Objective peak_allocated_bytes (bytes, minimize) is the process's PyTorch CUDA caching-allocator allocated peak for the single measured offline batch-32 forward: torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() queried outside the timer after the synchronized call, starting from the pre-call reset; it is not whole-GPU memory, not the reserved pool, and excludes NCCL/driver allocations (resnet_inference.py:43,48; README measurement section; adapter.py:126 reports it unchanged in metrics()).

Goal constraint: any measured solution on this same offline batch-32 workload must keep images_per_second >= 0.95 x the original baseline's images_per_second (workloads.json offline memory goal notation images_per_second_min_baseline_ratio 0.95, expressed generically as images_per_second >= 0.95 x baseline; request objective.constraints; request note on constraint conversion).

Metric scope: latency_ms remains recorded by the frozen evaluator (adapter.py:124) and images_per_second = batch(32) * 1e3 / latency_ms remains its exact reciprocal on the same frozen workload -- neither is an independent second goal of this variant, and reciprocal metrics must not be presented as separate goals (adapter.py:125; README section 6); peak_allocated_bytes is the only objective metric.
eval() mode is required for the measured forward: no dropout and no BatchNorm running-statistics updates (resnet_inference.py:23 .eval(); adapter.py:51,75).

Single process, world_size 1, on one CUDA device: no distributed backend, no NCCL collectives and no torch_communication metrics for this workload; peak_allocated_bytes is the single process's allocated peak with no cross-rank aggregation (request devices, distributed_backend null; request note on single process; README measurement section on per-process peak).

State protocol is unchanged: prepare() applies the configure() policy, loads the pinned FP32 weights locally from request['assets'], stages images on the device and builds pixels once; reset() restores torch.manual_seed(20261020) and re-asserts eval() outside timing and clears nothing (the source clears no gradients or caches inside its timed call) and does not touch any process group; run() holds no request-local mutable state; models() exposes {'model': <root ResNetForImageClassification module>}; set_mode and before_run are not implemented (adapter.py:42-75,132-133; original state_protocol).

The evaluator is frozen and executes unchanged (original contract frozen_files opop_adapter.py, opop_evaluate.py); its metrics() already emits peak_allocated_bytes, images_per_second and latency_ms (adapter.py:120-129), so the memory goal requires no adapter generation or edit, no invented measurement and no measurement-code change.

No accuracy or convergence claim beyond these reference-fidelity checks: the three fixture images are a correctness fixture, not an ImageNet evaluation (asset-manifest.json scope; common.py:58 quality_scope).
